gloss: right and wrong; good and evil

definitions.gloss: right and wrong; good and evil; justice and injustice
definitions.explanation: A formal compound contrasting the morally correct ({正|せい}) with the morally wrong ({邪|じゃ}). Used in writing and serious discussion to refer to the distinction itself.

examples.japanese: {正邪|せいじゃ}を{見極|みきわ}める。
{正邪|せいじゃ}の{判断|はんだん}は{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: Judging right and wrong is difficult.

examples.japanese: {裁判所|さいばんしょ}は{法|ほう}に{基|もと}づいて{正邪|せいじゃ}を{判定|はんてい}する。
examples.english: Courts determine right and wrong based on the law.

notes:
A formal, written-Japanese compound. In everyday speech, {善悪|ぜんあく} (good and evil) is more common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {正邪|せいじゃ}を{判断|はんだん}する: to judge right and wrong
- {正邪|せいじゃ}を{見極|みきわ}める: to discern right from wrong
- {正邪|せいじゃ}の{区別|くべつ}: the distinction between right and wrong

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {善悪|ぜんあく}: good and evil — more common, used in both speech and writing
- {是非|ぜひ}: rights and wrongs; whether to do something — also means 'by all means' as an adverb
